questions.q: Why does the churn workflow pin Python to 3.10 instead of using the newest version?
options: Because GitHub Actions only supports Python 3.10
Because CI should run the same stack as training and the Docker image, and the pinned scikit-learn 1.1.2 supports up to 3.10
Because newer Python versions cannot run pytest
Because caching only works with 3.10
questions.explain: Matching the Python version to the training environment and Docker base image keeps CI faithful to production; the pinned scikit-learn version limits which Python versions work.

questions.q: What does `cache: pip` in actions/setup-python do?
options: It saves the trained model between runs
It uploads test results as an artifact
It restores pip's download cache between runs, keyed on your dependency files
It disables installing packages
questions.explain: The cache speeds up dependency installation. It does not store models or test results.

questions.q: A second job needs the model trained in the first job. What is the right way to hand it over?
options: Assume the file is still on the runner
Upload it as an artifact in the first job and download it in the second
Commit the model file to main from inside CI
Retrain it by hand later
questions.explain: Each job runs on a clean machine, so files must travel as artifacts (or through another store).

questions.q: In the lesson's local check, a pull request with LogisticRegression(C=0.01) changed test AUC only from 0.802 to 0.799. What caught the change?
options: The golden-customer test, whose score fell from 0.909 to about 0.805
The schema test
The YAML parser
Nothing caught it
questions.explain: A behavior test can catch shifts that an aggregate metric like AUC barely shows.

questions.q: What did the lesson say about whether the workflow was run on GitHub?
options: It ran there and passed
It ran there and failed
It was not run on GitHub; the file was parsed with PyYAML and its steps were run locally in a clean copy
It was run on Docker Hub
questions.explain: Being clear about what was verified matters: the local run checks the commands, not GitHub's hosted execution.
